legend: The tumours commonly demonstrate a multilobulated or plexiform growth pattern.
Morphological clues to these tumours are inconsistent but include well-developed, almost circular nests of epithelioid cells, sometimes with pale or vacuolated cytoplasm {31789631}.
This tumour is indistinguishable morphologically from other pituitary adenomas / PitNETs.

In contrast to pulmonary hamartoma, the pulmonary chondromas associated with Carney triad do not show entrapped respiratory epithelium between the lobules of cartilage and do not contain other mesenchymal elements such as fat, smooth muscle, or myxoid spindle cells.
